question: Which of the following manifestations is LESS likely in tubulo-interstitial nephritis ?:

options.opa: Proteinuria greater than 3.5 g in 24 hours.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Tubulo-interstitial nephritis" -> "interstitial inflammation" -> "tubular damage" -> "impaired reabsorption" -> "nephrogenic diabetes insipidus" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Tubulo-interstitial nephritis" -> "interstitial inflammation" -> "tubular damage" -> "impaired acid-base balance" -> "renal tubular acidosis" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Tubulo-interstitial nephritis" -> "interstitial inflammation" -> "tubular damage" -> "impaired renal function" -> "progressive renal failure" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Tubulo-interstitial nephritis" -> "interstitial inflammation" -> "tubular damage" -> "impaired protein reabsorption" -> "proteinuria" -> "less than 3.5 g in 24 hours" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Tubulo-interstitial nephritis" -> "glomerular sparing" -> "less likely massive proteinuria" -> "proteinuria greater than 3.5 g in 24 hours less likely" -> 95%
analysis: Tubulo-interstitial nephritis is characterized by inflammation of the renal tubules and interstitium, often leading to impaired tubular function. Common manifestations include nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, renal tubular acidosis, and progressive renal failure due to tubular damage. However, significant proteinuria greater than 3.5 g in 24 hours is more characteristic of glomerular diseases, such as nephrotic syndrome, rather than tubulo-interstitial nephritis.
